intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without the tourist markup. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival Day 1, as the market is lively from early morning and located centrally near most mid-range hotel hubs.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Anime Immersion
experiences.description: Dive into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture in Akihabara. Visit multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, and themed cafes. Explore stores like Yodobashi Camera and independent retro game shops. This area is centrally located and easily accessible, making it a great afternoon activity even after a late arrival the night before.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in Asakusa, strolling through Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks. Experience the morning ritual atmosphere with incense and prayers. Asakusa is a central hub with many well-priced hotels nearby, making this a convenient and culturally rich morning experience across multiple days.

experiences.name: Shibuya Crossing & Izakaya Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at peak evening hours, then wind down with a traditional izakaya dinner featuring yakitori, edamame, and local craft beers. Shibuya is a major transit hub with abundant hotel options, making it ideal for travelers wanting to stay close to activity centers and avoid long commutes after late-night outings.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, a cutting-edge digital art museum blending technology and culture through interactive, boundary-dissolving installations. This experience perfectly bridges Tokyo's tech culture and artistic heritage. Book tickets in advance to secure entry. The Azabudai Hills location is accessible from central Tokyo hotels within 20-30 minutes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or train to Chiyoda City (approx. ¥1,000–¥3,000). Check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens — free entry, stunning cherry blossom aftermath in mid-April, and a peaceful introduction to Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Marunouchi Naka-dori avenue, admire the illuminated buildings, and explore the underground Yaesu or Tokyo Station food halls (Depachika) for an affordable dinner. Great chance to grab a bento or ramen bowl and get your first taste of Tokyo food culture.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Tokyo Station's Ramen Street (basement level) — bowls from ¥850–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Depachika (department store basement food hall) at Tokyo Station — pick up a discounted bento box (¥500–¥800) or try a standing sushi bar

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport or Tokyo Station — essential for budget travel on trains and buses throughout the trip. Download Google Maps offline for Tokyo. April 15 may still have late cherry blossoms depending on the year.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at Tsukiji Outer Market (30 min from Chiyoda by subway) — walk the stalls, sample fresh tamagoyaki (egg omelette skewers ¥200), try fresh seafood on a stick, and soak in the lively local food culture. Arrive early (8:00–9:00) for the best atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara Electric Town (10 min from Chiyoda) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Browse multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Akiba, explore retro game shops, manga stores, and maid café culture. Window shopping is completely free and endlessly entertaining.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening exploration. Visit the upper floors of Yodobashi or explore the back alleys for cheap izakaya (Japanese pub) dining. Try a set meal (teishoku) at a local chain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh fish on rice, tamagoyaki, and green tea (¥500–¥800 total)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a curry rice set at CoCo Ichibanya or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya/Matsuya (¥500–¥700)
meals.dinner: Akihabara izakaya — look for happy hour deals; order yakitori skewers and draft beer for ¥1,500–¥2,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is especially vibrant on weekday afternoons. Many electronics stores have tax-free shopping for tourists — bring your passport. Avoid buying electronics impulsively; prices can be compared online.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (20 min from Chiyoda) — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive by 8:30 before the crowds. Walk through the Kaminarimon Gate, explore Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional snacks and souvenirs, and enjoy the historic atmosphere. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River to Tokyo Skytree (15 min walk from Senso-ji). Admire the tower from the outside (free) and explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for food and local goods. Optionally take the free elevator to the 4th floor observation lobby area.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Ueno area (15 min from Asakusa). Explore Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air street market with food stalls, cheap clothing, and cosmetics. Great for budget shopping and street food snacking.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa — try ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and melon bread from Nakamise stalls (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Solamachi food court at Tokyo Skytree base — ramen, soba, or donburi sets (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market street food — grilled scallops, takoyaki octopus balls, and yakitori skewers (¥800–¥1,200 for a full street food dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most atmospheric in the early morning. Mid-April weather is mild (15–20°C) — a light jacket is recommended for evenings. Ameyoko closes around 20:00 so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku (25 min from Chiyoda). Walk the iconic Takeshita Street for quirky fashion, crepes, and youth culture. Then visit the serene Meiji Shrine (free entry) hidden in a forested area — a perfect contrast of tradition and modernity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Harajuku down Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's elegant tree-lined avenue. Window shop the flagship stores and admire the architecture. Head into the Omotesando Hills complex to browse (no need to buy). Then hop over to Shibuya (10 min walk) and witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shibuya at night — visit the free observation deck at Shibuya Sky's nearby Mag's Park or simply enjoy the energy of the crossing from the Starbucks overlooking it. Explore Shibuya Center-gai for budget dining and nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku — iconic Harajuku crepe from a street stall (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Omotesando area — find a basement café or try a Japanese sandwich (sando) from a convenience store (7-Eleven, Lawson) for ¥400–¥600
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen for a solo ramen booth experience (¥980–¥1,300) or Gyukaku yakiniku happy hour

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Takeshita Street will be very crowded — go before 11:00 for a better experience. The Meiji Shrine forest walk is calming and free. Shibuya Scramble is best photographed from the Mag's Park or Starbucks window on the second floor of the building facing the crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially in mid-April when late cherry blossoms or tulips may still be blooming. Spend 2–3 hours walking the French, English, and Japanese garden sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district and Golden Gai — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars with just 5–6 seats each. Browse the area freely in the afternoon. Visit Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori restaurants near Shinjuku Station West Exit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Omoide Yokocho — sit at a tiny counter, order yakitori skewers and a cold beer while surrounded by smoky, nostalgic Tokyo atmosphere. Then explore the neon lights of Shinjuku East Side.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby convenience store — onigiri rice balls and miso soup (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic — pick up a bento from a nearby convenience store and eat in the garden (¥500–¥700)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — yakitori set with beer (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays. Alcohol is allowed in the garden for picnics — a very local thing to do on weekends. Golden Gai bars are mostly open from evening; a drink in one tiny bar costs ¥500–¥1,000 with a small cover charge.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Odaiba (40 min from Chiyoda via Yurikamome monorail — scenic ride!). Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book in advance — ¥3,200). These are world-famous immersive digital art museums perfectly aligned with tech and culture interests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Odaiba — visit the free outdoor Statue of Liberty replica, enjoy views of Rainbow Bridge, and browse Diver City Tokyo Plaza (free entry) which houses a life-size Gundam statue outside — a must for tech and anime culture fans.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Visit Ginza (near Chiyoda) for a free evening stroll — admire the upscale architecture and window shop. Many galleries in Ginza offer free entry in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — tamagoyaki sandwich and coffee (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Odaiba — Diver City food court or the Aqua City mall food floor; try a seafood bowl (¥900–¥1,300)
meals.dinner: Ginza — find a standing sushi bar (tachinomi) or a ramen shop away from the main boulevard for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets online well in advance — they sell out quickly. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a highlight with great views of Tokyo Bay. Odaiba is a great example of Tokyo's futuristic urban planning and tech culture.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Shinjuku by budget JR/Tobu train — ¥1,400 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, colorful, and set in a forested mountain landscape. The main areas are free; the inner shrine costs ¥1,300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple, Futarasan Shrine, and the famous Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (free to view, ¥300 to walk across). Walk along the cedar-lined Nikko avenues.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax at the hotel or take a quiet walk around the Imperial Palace moat (always beautiful at night with reflections in the water).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or train station convenience store before departure (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Nikko — try yuba (tofu skin) dishes, a local specialty; set lunch at a small restaurant near the shrine (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Back in Chiyoda — try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal at a local restaurant near the hotel (¥900–¥1,300)

day_by_day.notes: Use the Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa Station for the most budget-friendly option. A Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,500 round trip including unlimited bus rides in Nikko) can save money. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking on uneven stone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (¥630 entry) — excellent exhibits on Japanese technology, robotics history, natural history, and science. A perfect intersection of tech culture and Japanese history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park (free) — stroll past Ueno Zoo (optional ¥600 entry), Shinobazu Pond with lotus flowers, and the open-air art stalls. Visit the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for a deep dive into Japanese cultural artifacts, samurai armor, and traditional arts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (10 min from Ueno) for a second evening visit — this time focus on the retro gaming arcades and explore the upper floors of multi-story game centers. Many arcade games cost only ¥100 per play.

meals.breakfast: Ueno area — try a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a kissaten (old-school coffee shop) near Ueno Station (¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Ueno Park — convenience store bento or grab street food from the park vendors (¥500–¥700)
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a maid café for the cultural experience (budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 including a drink and performance) or a cheap ramen shop

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Nature and Science has a fantastic permanent exhibit on Japanese innovation and robotics. Ueno Park is free and often hosts food festivals in April. Arcade gaming in Akihabara is a genuine local pastime — very budget-friendly entertainment.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's last remaining old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse antique shops, visit the old cemetery, and explore traditional craft stores. This area survived WWII bombing and feels like old Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller, less touristy version of Kyoto's Fushimi Inari with hundreds of torii gates. Then head to Nishi-Nippori for panoramic rooftop views of the Yanaka area from the free observation spot.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Shibuya or Shimokitazawa (30 min) — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage fashion, live music, and independent cafés. Walk the narrow streets and enjoy the alternative culture scene.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — try fresh-baked melon pan bread and croquettes from local bakeries (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — a small local teishoku restaurant for a set meal with rice, miso soup, and grilled fish (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — explore the many small independent restaurants; try a curry restaurant or a casual pasta bar (¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot without a strict plan — getting slightly lost is part of the charm. Shimokitazawa has a great live music scene; many small venues charge ¥1,000–¥2,000 cover and include a drink. Check listings for live shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not visited on Day 6) or explore the Toyosu Fish Market — the modern replacement for Tsukiji's inner market. Book a tuna auction viewing in advance (free but limited spots) or simply tour the outer market area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower, which combines contemporary art with a free city observation deck offering panoramic Tokyo views. Then explore the National Art Center (free entry to building, exhibitions vary).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roppongi for the evening — visit the free outdoor areas of Roppongi Hills and the Mori Garden. Roppongi has many international restaurants and a lively Friday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Toyosu or hotel area — fresh sushi breakfast at Toyosu Market (¥1,000–¥1,500 for a quality sushi set)
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills food floor — wide variety of options from ¥800–¥1,200; try Japanese curry or a donburi bowl
meals.dinner: Roppongi — find a budget-friendly Japanese restaurant away from the main tourist strip; try a shabu-shabu all-you-can-eat place (¥1,500–¥2,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View combo ticket is worth it for the views alone. Friday evenings in Roppongi are lively but can be expensive — stick to Japanese restaurants over Western ones for better value. The Mori Garden is free and beautifully lit at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line — ¥920 one way). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in) — a massive outdoor bronze Buddha statue (¥300 entry). Then hike the Daibutsu Trail through bamboo forest to Zeniarai Benzaiten Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hase-dera Temple (¥400) with its beautiful hillside gardens and ocean views. Walk along Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and souvenirs. Try shirasu (whitebait fish) dishes — a Kamakura specialty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Spend the evening in Shinjuku or Shibuya — explore a standing bar (tachinomi) for budget drinks and socialize with locals.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before train departure (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu don (whitebait rice bowl) at a local restaurant near Hase Station (¥1,000–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: Tokyo — standing bar (tachinomi) near Shinjuku; draft beer and small plates for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura can be very crowded on weekends in April — arrive early (first train around 8:00). The Daibutsu Hiking Trail is free and takes about 1.5 hours; wear comfortable shoes. JR Pass holders can use their pass for the Yokosuka Line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000) if not done earlier, or explore the quieter Hongo and Bunkyo neighborhoods — home to Tokyo University (free to walk the campus) and the historic Yushima Seido Confucian Temple (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Koenji or Nakameguro — two of Tokyo's most beloved local neighborhoods. Koenji is known for vintage shops and indie culture; Nakameguro is famous for its canal-side cafés and independent boutiques. The Meguro River walk is beautiful in spring.
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner night — treat yourself to a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) experience at a chain like Sushiro or Kura Sushi (¥100–¥150 per plate). A filling and fun dinner for ¥1,500–¥2,500. Then explore the area around your hotel one last time.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a traditional kissaten coffee shop — morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nakameguro canal-side café — sandwich or pasta set with coffee (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi conveyor belt sushi at Sushiro or Kura Sushi (¥1,500–¥2,500 for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: The Meguro River in Nakameguro is one of Tokyo's most Instagrammed spots — especially beautiful with late spring flowers. Koenji has excellent vintage clothing shops if you're looking for affordable unique souvenirs. Sunday afternoons in these neighborhoods have a relaxed, local vibe.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit your favorite spot or explore anywhere missed. The Imperial Palace East Gardens (free, opens 9:00) near the hotel is a perfect peaceful farewell walk. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from a 100-yen shop (Daiso) or the underground Yaesu shopping mall at Tokyo Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Store luggage at the hotel or at coin lockers in Tokyo Station (¥400–¥700). Take the train or bus to the airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transit and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days of food, tech, and culture in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Tokyo breakfast — a bowl of soba noodles at a standing noodle bar in Tokyo Station (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Airport — Narita or Haneda airport food courts have surprisingly good and affordable Japanese food; try a final ramen or tonkatsu set (¥900–¥1,400)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Leave extra time on the last day for any last-minute shopping or unexpected delays. Narita Express (N'EX) from Tokyo Station costs ¥3,070 one way; the Keikyu or Keio bus options are cheaper at ¥1,000–¥1,500. Don't forget to use up remaining Suica card balance on food or transfer it back to cash at a station machine.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City. Check in to the Chiyoda City Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen), a short stroll from most Chiyoda hotels. Enjoy the spring scenery and decompress after the flight. Visit the Nijubashi Bridge for iconic views of the Imperial Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Marunouchi Brick Square area as the sun sets, then head to the lively Yurakucho alley izakayas under the train tracks for your first authentic Tokyo evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a convenience store snack (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) upon arrival — excellent onigiri and sandwiches for under ¥500
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick bento from a depachika (department store basement food hall) at Tokyo Station — try Marunouchi Building's basement level
meals.dinner: Yurakucho Yakitori Alley — grilled skewers and cold beer at one of the retro izakayas under the train tracks, budget ¥2,000–3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: April is cherry blossom season — if blossoms are still out, the Imperial Palace gardens will be stunning. Keep the evening light as jet lag will likely set in. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport or Tokyo Station for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Arrive early (by 8:30am) to beat crowds. Walk Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs. Climb the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center observation deck for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Sumida River via the Azuma Bridge and visit teamLab Planets or the Sumida Hokusai Museum for a dose of tech-meets-culture. Alternatively, explore the Kappabashi Kitchen Town street for unique Japanese kitchenware and food-replica shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) — a short train ride from Asakusa — for an immersive dive into Tokyo's legendary tech and otaku culture. Browse multi-floor electronics stores, retro game shops, and manga cafes.

meals.breakfast: Café Komeda or a kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel for morning toast set — ¥600–900
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — famous sukiyaki and shabu-shabu at a more affordable lunch set, or try Sometaro okonomiyaki restaurant for a hands-on experience, ¥1,200–2,000
meals.dinner: Akihabara — dine at a themed maid café for the cultural experience, or grab a hearty ramen at Fuunji-style tsukemen shop nearby, ¥900–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. teamLab Planets tickets should be booked online in advance (¥3,200 adults). Akihabara is best experienced in the evening when neon lights come alive. Many electronics stores stay open until 21:00–22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market for a world-class food experience — sample fresh tamagoyaki (egg rolls), uni (sea urchin), and tuna sashimi from market stalls. This is a must for local food lovers. Arrive by 8:00am for the freshest selections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on the water. Enjoy matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) at the Nakajima Teahouse. Then cross Tokyo Bay by water bus to Odaiba for futuristic waterfront views.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Odaiba — visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue), browse the tech-forward teamLab digital art installations nearby, and enjoy the rainbow bridge night views from the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls — fresh sushi breakfast, tamagoyaki, and grilled scallops, budget ¥1,500–2,500 grazing
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu area — bento from a nearby convenience store eaten in the garden, or a light set lunch at a Shiodome restaurant, ¥1,000–1,500
meals.dinner: Odaiba Aqua City or DiverCity food floor — wide range of mid-range Japanese restaurants including ramen, tempura, and sushi sets, ¥1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is free to walk through — just be mindful of stall vendors and keep pathways clear. Book teamLab Borderless Odaiba tickets online (¥3,200). The water bus from Hamarikyu to Odaiba is a scenic and fun ¥480 ride.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Park — one of Tokyo's most beloved green spaces, especially beautiful in cherry blossom season. Explore the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest, housing over 110,000 cultural artifacts) for a deep dive into Japanese art, history, and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Ueno — visit the National Museum of Nature and Science or stroll Ameyoko Market, a lively open-air bazaar with street food, clothing, and fresh produce. Great for local market culture and budget shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Crossing scramble experience at night. Visit the free Shibuya Sky observation deck (book in advance) or the Mag's Park rooftop for aerial views of the crossing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten morning set — Japanese-style with miso soup, rice, and grilled fish, ¥700–1,200
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — yakitori, takoyaki, and fresh fruit stalls, budget ¥800–1,500 grazing
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try Ichiran Ramen (solo dining booths, iconic experience) or Genki Sushi (conveyor belt sushi), ¥1,200–2,200

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum entry is ¥1,000 for adults. Ueno Park itself is free. Shibuya Sky observation deck costs ¥2,000 and should be booked online. Saturday evenings make Shibuya Crossing especially electric — arrive around 19:00–20:00 for peak energy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (90 minutes by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa) — a UNESCO World Heritage site featuring the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine, colorful pagodas, and cedar forests. Arrive by 9:30am to maximize time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple, the Sacred Bridge (Shinkyo), and hike up to Taiyuin Mausoleum. The mountain air and elaborate architecture offer a stunning contrast to urban Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (aim to be back by 18:30). Relax near the hotel or explore the Kanda/Jimbocho neighborhood — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district, great for browsing vintage books, maps, and prints.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast or hotel — keep it quick for the early train departure
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local specialty. Try Gyoshintei restaurant or a yuba set lunch at a local restaurant near the shrines, ¥1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Jimbocho or Kanda area — curry is a Jimbocho tradition; try Bondy or Nair's Restaurant for Japanese-style curry, ¥1,200–2,000

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass (¥4,780 from Asakusa) for round-trip train and local bus access — excellent value. Nikko shrines charge separate entry fees totaling approximately ¥1,300 for the main complex. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Nikko's uneven stone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Walk the Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent craft shops, and visit the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery, known for its cherry blossoms and peaceful ambiance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Nezu Shrine — a beautiful vermilion torii gate tunnel similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded. Then explore the Sendagi and Nezu area's charming backstreets, traditional wooden houses, and independent cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara for a deeper tech culture experience — visit Yodobashi Camera's massive multi-floor store, explore retro game arcades (Game Centers), and browse Gundam Base or Kotobukiya figure shops. End the night at a manga kissa (manga café) for a uniquely Japanese experience.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh melon pan (sweet bread) from a local bakery, ¥200–400
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — a traditional shokudo (Japanese diner) for a teishoku set meal (rice, miso soup, protein, pickles), ¥850–1,400
meals.dinner: Akihabara — try a multi-floor izakaya chain like Torikizoku (all items ¥350) for affordable yakitori and drinks, or Gyukatsu Motomura for crispy beef katsu, ¥1,200–2,000

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The area gives a rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo architecture. Nezu Shrine is free to enter. Akihabara game centers are open until midnight — great for experiencing Japanese gaming culture firsthand.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Harajuku — start with the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine, set within a 70-hectare forested park. A peaceful contrast to the city's energy. Participate in a morning ritual if timing aligns, and explore the forested walking paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for Harajuku's famous youth fashion and crepe culture, then transition to the upscale Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — for architecture, design boutiques, and the Omotesando Hills complex. Visit the Prada and Louis Vuitton buildings for their architectural merit alone.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish neighborhoods. Walk the Meguro River (especially beautiful if late cherry blossoms remain), browse the iconic Tsutaya Books (Daikanyama T-Site), and enjoy the trendy café and bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku — a fresh crepe from Marion Crepes on Takeshita Street, ¥500–800, or a café breakfast at a nearby kissaten
meals.lunch: Omotesando — Maisen Tonkatsu (famous pork cutlet in a converted bathhouse), lunch set ¥1,500–2,200
meals.dinner: Nakameguro — riverside restaurant or wine bar; try Nakameguro Taproom (craft beer and food) or a cozy Italian bistro along the canal, ¥2,000–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter; the inner treasure museum costs ¥500. Omotesando is a great area for window shopping without spending. Nakameguro is especially atmospheric in the evening — the canal lighting creates a romantic, cinematic atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (if not yet visited) or explore the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art spaces with stunning city views from the Mori Tower observation deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (free admission to the building, Japan's largest exhibition space) and the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Midtown Tokyo, a design-focused museum by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo's upscale side with a walk through Azabu-Juban, a sophisticated neighborhood with excellent international dining. Alternatively, return to Roppongi for its legendary nightlife or a jazz bar experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Roppongi area café — try a French-style café morning set near Midtown Tokyo, ¥800–1,400
meals.lunch: National Art Center Tokyo's Brasserie Paul Bocuse Le Musée — iconic inverted cone restaurant inside the museum, lunch set ¥2,200–3,500 (a splurge worth the experience)
meals.dinner: Azabu-Juban — explore the neighborhood's diverse restaurant scene; try Niku no Mansei for wagyu beef or a mid-range sushi counter, ¥2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum + observation deck combo ticket is ¥2,000. 21_21 Design Sight entry is ¥1,200. Book the Brasserie Paul Bocuse lunch in advance — it's inside the National Art Center and is an architectural experience as much as a meal. Roppongi can be expensive at night — set a drink budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kamakura (about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line). Start with the iconic Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu) — a 13-meter bronze statue dating to 1252. Explore the surrounding Hase-dera Temple with its sea views and hydrangea gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Komachi-dori shopping street for local sweets and crafts, then hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and past smaller shrines to Zeniarai Benzaiten Ugafuku Shrine — where washing money is said to double it. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Spend the evening at the Kagurazaka neighborhood — Tokyo's former geisha district with French-Japanese cultural fusion, narrow stone-paved alleys (yokocho), and excellent dining.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — convenience store onigiri and canned coffee at the station, ¥400–600
meals.lunch: Kamakura — Hachi no Su café or a shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl restaurant near Hase Station; shirasu-don is a Kamakura specialty, ¥1,200–1,800
meals.dinner: Kagurazaka — a French-Japanese fusion bistro or a traditional kaiseki-lite restaurant; try La Ranarita or a local izakaya in the hidden alleys, ¥2,000–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is best explored with a day pass. Great Buddha entry is ¥300. Wear comfortable shoes for the hiking trail (approximately 2 hours, moderate difficulty). Kagurazaka is compact and best explored on foot — the hidden alleyways (横丁) are magical at night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (free, open from 9:00am) for panoramic city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Then walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Japan's finest landscape gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Shinjuku's electronics and camera culture on the west side (Yodobashi Camera flagship), then cross to the east side for Kabukicho, Tokyo's famous entertainment district. Visit the Robot Restaurant area and the multi-story Tokyu Hands for Japanese design and lifestyle goods.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Golden Gai — Shinjuku's legendary maze of over 200 tiny bars, each seating 5–8 people. This is one of Tokyo's most unique cultural experiences. Then explore Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) for smoky yakitori skewers in a post-war alley atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku — Tsunahachi Tempura for a tempura morning set, or a hotel breakfast, ¥900–1,500
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen area — a bento picnic eaten in the garden (buy from nearby convenience store or Isetan department store basement), ¥800–1,500
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — smoky yakitori skewers, cold beer, and a seat at a tiny counter bar; budget ¥2,000–3,000 for food and drinks

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500 (no alcohol allowed inside). Golden Gai bars typically charge a ¥500–1,000 seating fee (otoshi) on top of drinks — this is normal. Friday nights in Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho are particularly lively. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck closes at 22:30.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (or the newly opened Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum in Koganei if you want a full outdoor experience) — a comprehensive museum covering Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern times. Fascinating for understanding the city's cultural evolution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ryogoku — the sumo district. Visit the Kokugikan Sumo Arena (exterior and sumo museum, free), browse sumo-related shops, and try chanko-nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew) at a local restaurant. If a tournament is scheduled, book tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ginza for a sophisticated evening stroll — Tokyo's most upscale shopping district transforms into a pedestrian zone on weekends (Hokoten). Window shop at flagship stores, visit the Itoya stationery flagship (9 floors of Japanese stationery and design), and enjoy the elegant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Ryogoku area — a traditional Japanese breakfast at a local shokudo or hotel, ¥700–1,200
meals.lunch: Ryogoku — chanko-nabe set lunch at Yoshiba or Tomoegata (sumo stables-turned-restaurants), a culturally immersive dining experience, ¥1,500–2,500
meals.dinner: Ginza — mid-range sushi at Sushi Saito's area alternatives, or try Kyubey Ginza for accessible counter sushi, or a tempura restaurant; budget ¥2,500–4,000

day_by_day.notes: Edo-Tokyo Museum admission is ¥600. The Sumo Museum inside Kokugikan is free. Weekend Ginza Hokoten (pedestrian paradise) runs from 12:00–17:00 in spring/summer. April sumo tournament (Natsu Basho) typically runs in May — check the exact 2027 schedule for possible overlap.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Odaiba area for a tech-culture morning — explore the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), Japan's premier science and technology museum featuring ASIMO robots, space exploration exhibits, and cutting-edge digital displays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Tokyo and explore the Akihabara retro gaming scene more deeply — visit Super Potato (vintage game store), Trader (retro electronics), and the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for figures and collectibles. End with a visit to the UDX building's tech events if any are running.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening experience — visit the Shibuya Sky or Tokyo Skytree observation deck for a breathtaking night panorama of Tokyo's 37-million-person megalopolis. Tokyo Skytree (634 meters, world's tallest tower) offers unparalleled views.

meals.breakfast: Odaiba — a café breakfast at Palette Town or a convenience store option near the waterfront, ¥600–1,000
meals.lunch: Miraikan area — the museum café or a nearby Odaiba restaurant; try a Japanese family restaurant (Denny's Japan or Gusto) for a local chain experience, ¥1,000–1,600
meals.dinner: Asakusa (near Skytree) — Mugitoro restaurant for tororo (mountain yam) cuisine, or a traditional tempura restaurant; budget ¥2,000–3,500

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan entry is ¥630 — book robot demonstration time slots upon arrival. Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck entry is ¥2,100 (Tembo Galleria additional ¥1,000) — book online to avoid queues. Sunday evenings at Skytree are busy; aim to arrive by 17:30 for sunset views transitioning to night views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit a favorite neighborhood or tick off any remaining items. Consider a quiet morning at the Imperial Palace East Gardens or a final walk through Chiyoda's Hibiya Park. Visit the Intermediatheque museum (free, inside KITTE building at Tokyo Station) for a curated collection of Tokyo University's cultural artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping at KITTE (former central post office, now a curated shopping complex with excellent Japanese craft and food brands) or the Tokyo Station Character Street for unique souvenirs. Visit the Tokyo Station Gallery for a final cultural stop. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Marunouchi or Nihonbashi area — close to the hotel for a relaxed final evening. Reflect on 13 days of Tokyo exploration.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final kissaten morning set — savor the Japanese coffee shop ritual one last time, ¥700–1,200
meals.lunch: KITTE basement food hall or Tokyo Station Ramen Street — try a regional ramen style you haven't had yet (Sapporo miso, Hakata tonkotsu, or Kitakata shoyu), ¥900–1,500
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi — Taimeiken Western-style yoshoku restaurant (famous for omurice and hayashi rice, a Tokyo institution since 1931), ¥1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: KITTE's Intermediatheque is free and open until 20:00 (closed Mondays — check 2027 schedule). Allow at least 3 hours for airport transfer — Narita Express takes 60 minutes from Tokyo Station. Purchase any last Suica card balance refunds at the station. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping refunds at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without the tourist markup. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival Day 1, as the market is lively from early morning and located centrally near most mid-range hotel hubs.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-in: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Narita/Haneda to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay via private luxury car service (pre-arrange through hotel concierge). Settle in, freshen up, and receive a welcome briefing from the concierge on your 13-day itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi-Gyoen), a serene 28-acre garden adjacent to Chiyoda. Stroll along the moat, admire the stone walls and spring blooms, and decompress from the long flight. Visit the Sannomaru Shozokan (Museum of the Imperial Collections) if open.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kanda (3 Michelin stars, Chiyoda area) — an intimate 8-seat counter helmed by Chef Hiroyuki Kanda offering exquisite kaiseki cuisine. Book well in advance. After dinner, a quiet nightcap at the New Bar in the Palace Hotel Tokyo overlooking the Imperial Palace moat.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or at airport upon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light bento or ramen at a quality spot near Narita/Haneda airport during transit, or room service upon check-in at the boutique stay
meals.dinner: Kaiseki multi-course dinner at Kanda (3 Michelin stars, Chiyoda) — expect seasonal ingredients, pristine dashi broths, and impeccable presentation. Budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag management: keep dinner light and retire early. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm all upcoming reservations. April in Tokyo means cherry blossom season may still be lingering — confirm bloom status upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour: Begin at 8:00 AM with a guided premium food tour of Tsukiji Outer Market (15 min taxi from Chiyoda). Sample fresh uni (sea urchin), hand-rolled tamagoyaki, premium tuna sashimi, dashi-infused street snacks, and artisan pickles. Visit specialty vendors including Yamagishi Eggs and Tsukiji Tamagoyaki Marutake. Pair with freshly brewed Japanese green tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ginza for an exploration of Japan's most prestigious shopping district. Visit the flagship Itoya stationery store (9 floors of artisan paper goods), browse the Ginza Six luxury mall, and stop into the Sony Park or Apple Ginza for a taste of Tokyo's tech retail culture. Visit the Hermès Maison Ginza building — the glass facade is an architectural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza, 3 Michelin stars) — the world-famous sushi counter of Jiro Ono. Reservations are extraordinarily difficult; book through hotel concierge months ahead. If unavailable, dine at Saito (Ginza, 2 Michelin stars) for exceptional nigiri. After dinner, visit the Ginza bar scene — Bar High Five on 4F of Efflore Ginza is one of Tokyo's finest cocktail bars.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market street food tasting — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and green tea (included in food tour)
meals.lunch: Kappo-style lunch at Kyubey Ginza — a legendary tempura and sushi institution open for lunch sets (¥8,000–¥15,000)
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sukiyabashi Jiro or Saito, Ginza (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person). 20 precise nigiri courses in under 30 minutes — pure, focused excellence

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji food tour is best on an empty stomach — eat lightly beforehand. Wear comfortable shoes for market walking. Ginza shops typically open at 11:00 AM. Confirm Jiro reservation status with concierge on Day 1.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive: Take the JR Yamanote Line or taxi to Akihabara (10 min from Chiyoda). Explore the epicenter of Tokyo's tech and electronics culture. Visit Yodobashi Akiba (8-floor electronics megastore), browse retro gaming at Super Potato, and explore the latest in robotics, components, and gadgets at Radio Kaikan. Visit the Gundam Café and Evangelion Store for anime-tech crossover culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island — take the Yurikamome monorail for scenic bay views. Interact with ASIMO-era robots, explore AI and space exhibits, and see the Geo-Cosmos globe. Afterward, stroll the futuristic Odaiba waterfront with views of the Rainbow Bridge and a replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu Garden Place, 3 Michelin stars) — take a taxi to Ebisu for a lavish French-Japanese fusion experience in a château-style building. The tasting menu showcases Robuchon's legendary pommes purée alongside Japanese seasonal ingredients. Alternatively, dine at L'Effervescence (Nishiazabu) for inventive modern French cuisine with Japanese soul.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Chatei Hatou in Shibuya — a legendary old-school kissaten (coffee shop) serving hand-drip coffee and morning toast
meals.lunch: Ramen lunch at Fuunji (Shinjuku) — one of Tokyo's finest tsukemen (dipping ramen) spots. Expect a queue; arrive at 11:30 AM
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person). Grand wine pairing available. Dress code: smart elegant

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Miraikan requires advance ticket booking online. The Yurikamome monorail ride to Odaiba offers excellent city views — sit at the front car.

day_by_day.morning: Asakusa Cultural Immersion: Take a taxi or subway to Asakusa (15 min from Chiyoda). Arrive early at Senso-ji Temple for a peaceful experience before crowds gather. Participate in omikuji (fortune drawing) and browse the Nakamise-dori shopping street for premium artisan crafts — lacquerware, tenugui towels, and ningyo dolls. Visit the Asakusa Shrine and Denboin Garden (reserve in advance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private rickshaw (jinrikisha) tour through Asakusa's backstreets — arrange through hotel concierge for a 60–90 minute guided ride through old Shitamachi neighborhoods, past traditional townhouses, small shrines, and artisan workshops. Afterward, visit the Tokyo Skytree (634m) — book the premium Tembo Galleria (450m) for panoramic views of the entire Kanto plain.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Hyotei (if visiting their Tokyo branch) or Harutaka (Ginza, 2 Michelin stars) for an intimate omakase sushi experience. After dinner, take an evening stroll along the Sumida River waterfront — the illuminated Skytree and Azuma Bridge reflections are spectacular in spring.

meals.breakfast: Café Kamiya near Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest Western-style bar and café, serving morning coffee and toast in a historic 1880 setting
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura Asakusa — a 130-year-old institution serving sesame-oil-fried tempura don (¥3,000–¥5,000). Arrive early to avoid queues
meals.dinner: Omakase at Harutaka, Ginza (¥35,000–¥50,000 per person) — intimate 10-seat counter, exceptional seasonal nigiri

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most atmospheric at dawn or dusk. Rickshaw tours should be booked 1–2 days in advance. Skytree tickets can sell out on weekends — pre-book online. April evenings can be cool; bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka & Nezu Neighborhood Walk: Explore one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods, a 20-min taxi from Chiyoda. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (cherry blossom stragglers may remain), browse the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (old-fashioned shopping street), and visit the Yanaka Sculpture Garden. Stop at artisan shops selling handmade pottery, calligraphy brushes, and traditional sweets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (15 min walk from Yanaka) — the largest art museum in Japan. Explore the Honkan (Japanese Gallery) for samurai armor, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient ceramics. Book a private curator-led tour through the hotel for an elevated experience. Afterward, stroll through Ueno Park and visit the Toshogu Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ukai-tei Omotesando — a premier teppanyaki restaurant where skilled chefs prepare A5 Wagyu beef, Hokkaido seafood, and seasonal vegetables on iron griddles before your eyes. The theatrical presentation and premium ingredients make this a memorable evening. Follow with drinks at the Peninsula Bar in the Peninsula Tokyo (Chiyoda area).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Kayaba Coffee in Yanaka — a beautifully restored 1938 coffee shop serving morning sets with egg sandwiches and pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Soba lunch at Kanda Yabu Soba — one of Tokyo's oldest and most revered soba restaurants (est. 1880), near Akihabara. Hand-cut buckwheat soba in refined dashi broth (¥2,000–¥4,000)
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki at Ukai-tei Omotesando (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person). A5 Wagyu course with seasonal accompaniments and sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays; Sunday is ideal. Ukai-tei requires advance reservation. The Peninsula Tokyo is a 5-min walk from the hotel area — excellent for a nightcap.

day_by_day.morning: teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills): Experience Japan's world-renowned digital art collective. teamLab Planets in Toyosu offers an immersive barefoot journey through water mirror rooms, crystal universes, and overgrown flower gardens. Book the first entry slot (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Alternatively, visit the newly reopened teamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills for a boundary-free art museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Roppongi Art Triangle: Take a taxi to Roppongi and explore the prestigious art district. Visit the Mori Art Museum (54th floor of Mori Tower) for contemporary art with sweeping city views from the Tokyo City View observation deck. Then walk to the National Art Center Tokyo for its stunning undulating glass facade and rotating major exhibitions. Finish at 21_21 Design Sight in Midtown.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin (Roppongi, 3 Michelin stars) — Chef Seiji Yamamoto's legendary kaiseki restaurant pushing the boundaries of traditional Japanese cuisine with modern techniques. Dishes may include liquid nitrogen preparations and sous-vide masterpieces alongside pristine seasonal ingredients. One of the most innovative dining experiences in the world.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Bread, Espresso & (Omotesando) — artisan bakery café known for exceptional pain de mie and single-origin espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Roppongi Hills Club or a casual bowl of premium tonkotsu at Ichiran Roppongi — individual booths for a focused, personal ramen experience (¥1,500–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Kaiseki at Ryugin, Roppongi (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person). Sake pairing curated by the sommelier is highly recommended

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be purchased online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on some days). Ryugin reservations open 1 month in advance online — set a calendar reminder.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko (UNESCO World Heritage): Depart Chiyoda at 8:00 AM via private luxury car or the Tobu Nikko Limited Express (Spacia X — Japan's most premium limited express train, book Green Car). Arrive in Nikko (~2 hours). Visit the breathtaking Toshogu Shrine complex — ornate Edo-period mausoleums, the Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight), and the sacred Shinkyobashi Bridge. Walk up to Taiyuinbyo Mausoleum for fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nikko National Park area — visit Kegon Falls (97m waterfall) and the turquoise Lake Chuzenji (accessible by car via the winding Irohazaka road). Walk along the lakeside and enjoy the mountain scenery. In late April, snowcapped peaks may still be visible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:00. Dinner at Nihonryori RyuGin's sibling or opt for a relaxed evening at Tempura Kondo (Ginza, 1 Michelin star) — Chef Fumio Kondo's legendary tempura counter where vegetables and seafood are fried to ethereal lightness. A more relaxed but equally refined evening after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or onigiri and green tea from a premium convenience store (7-Eleven Japan offers surprisingly excellent quality) for the train journey
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) kaiseki lunch at Gyoshintei restaurant within Nikko's Kanman-ga-fuchi Abyss area — a traditional Nikko specialty in a garden setting (¥5,000–¥12,000)
meals.dinner: Tempura omakase at Kondo, Ginza (¥25,000–¥35,000 per person). Seasonal vegetable and seafood tempura of extraordinary delicacy

day_by_day.notes: Book Spacia X train tickets online via Tobu Railway website. Nikko Toshogu can be crowded on weekdays in April — arrive early. Wear layers as Nikko's mountain areas are cooler than Tokyo. Confirm return train time with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku & Omotesando Cultural-Fashion Morning: Take a taxi to Harajuku (20 min from Chiyoda). Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine at 9:00 AM for a peaceful Shinto experience in a forested sanctuary — participate in the purification ritual at the temizuya. Walk through the forested approach path. Then explore Takeshita Street for Tokyo's most eccentric youth fashion and crepe culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Omotesando Hills & Designer Boutiques: Walk along Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées. Browse flagship stores by Japanese designers: Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons, Yohji Yamamoto, and Junya Watanabe. Visit the Prada Aoyama building (Herzog & de Meuron architecture) and the Nezu Museum (Japanese and Asian antiques in a stunning Kengo Kuma-designed building with a bamboo garden).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège (Minami-Aoyama, 2 Michelin stars) — Chef Hiroyasu Kawate's open-kitchen restaurant offering inventive French cuisine with Japanese ingredients and a strong philosophy of zero-waste cooking. The 10-seat counter facing the kitchen creates an intimate, theatrical experience. Follow with cocktails at Bar Benfiddich (Shinjuku) — Japan's most celebrated craft cocktail bar using house-made bitters and foraged ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Café de L'Ambre in Ginza — a legendary 1948 coffee house serving aged single-origin coffees. A Tokyo institution for coffee connoisseurs
meals.lunch: Afuri Ramen, Harajuku — yuzu-infused shio ramen in a sleek, modern space. One of Tokyo's most beloved ramen concepts (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Florilège (¥25,000–¥35,000 per person). Natural wine pairing curated by sommelier. Reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is most serene before 9:30 AM. Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in spring. Bar Benfiddich is tiny (8 seats) — no reservations taken, arrive early or expect a wait. Omotesando boutiques open at 11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Exploration — Tech & Culture: Take the JR Chuo Line to Shinjuku (15 min from Chiyoda). Visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, 202m) for panoramic views. Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district by day — visit Robot Restaurant area and the new Kabukicho Tower complex. Browse Kinokuniya Bookstore's international floor and Disk Union for rare Japanese vinyl.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden: One of Japan's finest landscape gardens combining French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional garden styles. In late April, late-blooming cherry varieties (Ichiyo, Kanzan) may still be visible alongside wisteria. The greenhouse contains tropical plants from Japan's southern islands. Afterward, explore the Golden Gai district's labyrinthine alleyways of tiny bars (best appreciated in the evening but fascinating to explore by day).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Nakamura (Shinjuku, traditional kaiseki) or Sushi Saito (if a rare reservation opens — considered by many the finest sushi in Japan, located in Akasaka). Alternatively, enjoy an evening in Shinjuku's Golden Gai — a warren of 200+ tiny bars, each seating 5–8 people. Choose a bar that matches your mood (jazz, classic rock, whisky, film). An unmissable Tokyo experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit a traditional Japanese breakfast set at Imahan Shinjuku — sukiyaki restaurant also serving morning kaiseki sets
meals.lunch: Wagyu beef lunch at Imahan Shinjuku or Shinjuku Kappo Nakamura — premium wagyu shabu-shabu in an elegant tatami setting (¥8,000–¥15,000)
meals.dinner: Golden Gai bar hopping — budget ¥3,000–¥8,000 per bar for drinks and small plates. Start at Albatross for its stunning 3-floor interior, then explore. Or: formal dinner at Nakamura Shinjuku (¥20,000–¥35,000)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entry fee (¥500). Alcohol is not permitted in the garden. Golden Gai bars typically have a small cover charge (¥500–¥1,000). Some bars are regulars-only — look for 'No 1st Visit' signs. The area is safe and welcoming to tourists in most venues.

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya Tech & Pop Culture: Take the Ginza Line to Shibuya. Start at the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — experience the organized chaos from street level and from the Scramble Square observation deck (Shibuya Sky, 229m) for aerial views. Visit Shibuya 109 for fast fashion culture, then explore the newly developed Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Cast areas — examples of Tokyo's urban regeneration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pokémon Center Shibuya and Nintendo Tokyo (in Shibuya Parco) for premium gaming merchandise — a must for tech culture enthusiasts. Explore Shibuya Parco's art floors and the GALLERY X. Then walk to Daikanyama — Tokyo's most stylish neighborhood — to browse the Tsutaya Books T-Site (a stunning bookstore-café complex in a bamboo-clad building) and the boutiques of Hillside Terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sézanne (Four Seasons Hotel Marunouchi, 2 Michelin stars) — Chef Daniel Calvert's exceptional French restaurant blending classical French technique with Japanese precision and seasonal ingredients. One of Tokyo's most celebrated dining destinations. After dinner, return to the hotel area for a nightcap at the Palace Hotel Tokyo's Crown Bar.

meals.breakfast: Streamer Coffee Company, Shibuya — Tokyo's pioneering specialty coffee bar known for latte art and single-origin pour-overs
meals.lunch: Curry lunch at Nakamura-ya Shinjuku (if traveling back through Shinjuku) or a premium katsu sando from Maisen Aoyama — Japan's finest tonkatsu in a converted bathhouse (¥2,000–¥4,000)
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Sézanne, Four Seasons Marunouchi (¥35,000–¥55,000 per person). Exceptional wine list with rare Burgundy and Champagne selections

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck tickets should be booked online in advance. Nintendo Tokyo and Pokémon Center can have queues on weekends — Friday afternoon is manageable. Tsutaya Books T-Site in Daikanyama is open until 24:00 — a magical late-night bookshop experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Hakone (Mt. Fuji Views): Depart Chiyoda at 7:30 AM via the Romancecar (Odakyu luxury limited express) from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto (~90 min). Transfer to the Hakone Ropeway for aerial views of Mt. Fuji (weather permitting) and the volcanic Owakudani sulfur vents. Visit Lake Ashi for iconic Fuji reflections and a traditional wooden boat cruise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum — Japan's first open-air art museum featuring sculptures by Picasso, Henry Moore, and Rodin set against mountain scenery. Afterward, indulge in a private onsen (hot spring) experience — book a private rotenburo (outdoor bath) at a premium ryokan such as Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu for a 2-hour session.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:30. Dinner at Aronia de Takazawa (Akasaka, 2 Michelin stars) — Chef Yoshiaki Takazawa's intimate 10-seat restaurant offering one of Tokyo's most creative and personal dining experiences, blending Japanese ingredients with avant-garde French techniques. A theatrical, emotional meal.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or ekiben (premium railway bento) purchased at Shinjuku Station for the Romancecar journey
meals.lunch: Soba lunch at Hakone Soba or a kaiseki bento at Gora Kadan's café — mountain soba with seasonal tempura in a scenic setting (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Omakase at Aronia de Takazawa (¥35,000–¥55,000 per person). Only 4 tables — one of Tokyo's hardest reservations. Book months ahead through concierge

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji is only visible in clear weather — April can be hazy. Check the Hakone Ropeway weather forecast the day before. The Romancecar has a premium car with panoramic front windows — book seat 1A or 1B. Private onsen session at Gora Kadan must be reserved in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Kagurazaka & Edo-Tokyo Cultural Morning: Walk or taxi to Kagurazaka (10 min from Chiyoda) — a former geisha district now home to French bistros, traditional Japanese restaurants, and artisan shops along cobblestone alleyways (yokocho). Visit Akagi Shrine (redesigned by architect Kengo Kuma) and browse the Kagurazaka shopping street for artisan ceramics, wagashi (Japanese sweets), and handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Edo-Tokyo Museum (Ryogoku): Take a taxi to Ryogoku to visit this spectacular museum chronicling Tokyo's transformation from Edo-period fishing village to modern megalopolis. Walk across a full-scale replica of Nihonbashi Bridge and explore dioramas, artifacts, and interactive exhibits. Nearby, visit the Kokugikan Sumo Arena — if a tournament is running in April, attend a session (January, May, September are official basho months, but training stables may offer visits).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Quintessence (Shirokanedai, 3 Michelin stars) — Chef Shuzo Kishida's landmark French restaurant, one of the most influential in Japan. A long-form tasting menu of extraordinary refinement, featuring French classical cuisine elevated by Japanese precision and seasonal ingredients. A perfect capstone to the culinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Akagi Café near Kagurazaka's Akagi Shrine — a stylish café within the shrine complex serving excellent coffee and morning pastries
meals.lunch: Wagashi (Japanese confectionery) tasting at Toraya Kagurazaka — Japan's most prestigious wagashi maker (est. 1526), serving seasonal sweets with matcha in an elegant tearoom (¥3,000–¥5,000)
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Quintessence, Shirokanedai (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person). One of Tokyo's greatest dining experiences. Advance reservation essential — book 2–3 months ahead

day_by_day.notes: Kagurazaka is especially charming on Sunday mornings before crowds arrive. The Edo-Tokyo Museum may have temporary exhibition surcharges — check the website. Quintessence has a strict no-phone-photography policy during service. Dress code: smart formal.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Chiyoda: Begin with a peaceful early morning walk around the Imperial Palace outer moat — the 5km perimeter walk is a Tokyo classic, popular with joggers and offers serene views of the palace walls, moat, and willow trees. Visit the Kitanomaru Park within the palace grounds and stop at the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping at Mitsukoshi Ginza or Isetan Shinjuku — Japan's finest department stores with exceptional basement food halls (depachika) for premium omiyage (souvenirs): artisan chocolates, premium dashi packs, wagashi, sake, and Japanese ceramics. Visit the Okashi Land candy floor and the artisan food marketplace. Pack carefully for the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations: Hotel checkout and private luxury car transfer to Narita or Haneda. Enjoy a final meal at the airport — Narita International Terminal has excellent Japanese restaurants including premium sushi and ramen counters. Alternatively, have an early farewell dinner near the hotel at Imahan (Ginza) for a final sukiyaki or shabu-shabu feast before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the Japanese breakfast option: grilled salmon, miso soup, tamagoyaki, rice, pickles, and natto if adventurous
meals.lunch: Depachika exploration lunch at Mitsukoshi Ginza — assemble a premium bento from the basement food hall: premium sashimi, wagyu croquettes, artisan onigiri, and seasonal pickles (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Airport farewell meal at Narita's Nadaman (traditional Japanese) or Ramen Street in the terminal — a final bowl of Tokyo-style ramen as a send-off

day_by_day.notes: Allow 3.5 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Narita; 3 hours for Haneda. Confirm private car transfer time with hotel concierge the evening before. Excess luggage from shopping: most hotels offer international luggage shipping (takuhaibin) directly to your home address — arrange 24 hours in advance. Japan's consumption tax (currently 10%) is refunded at airport tax-free counters for purchases over ¥5,000 — keep receipts.
